title: Code Reviewer operator API, version 1
description: The wire format of the operator API (#275, #278, #280, #284, #385): a machine interface for an operator who sets the entitlements of workspaces, reads what they consumed and redeems the handover of a workspace Owner or Admin, from outside the app. Every request carries 'Authorization: Bearer <OPERATOR_API_TOKEN>'; a request body is application/json up to 16384 bytes, and GET and DELETE carry none. Every answer is JSON with 'Cache-Control: no-store' and the version in its body; an error is {version, error, field?} with a stable code, never a message. Until OPERATOR_API_TOKEN is set the paths do not exist (the 404 of a missing path, not this format). The API identifies workspaces by id and slug only: no names of people, no emails, no repositories, no pull requests. A reader ignores fields it does not know. This file is the only source of the format; the app tests validate real answers and contracts/examples/operator-api holds one valid example per definition.

Version.description: The version of the format; also in the path (/api/operator/v1).

WorkspaceId.description: The id of a workspace, as listed by GET /workspaces.

ApiErrorCode.description: Callers branch on the code. 401 unauthorized; 404 not_found (unknown path) or workspace_not_found; 405 method_not_allowed (with an Allow header); 400 body_not_allowed (a GET or DELETE with a body), request_invalid (not JSON, or a bad query such as a limit out of range), cursor_invalid (a usage cursor that is not one of the API's) or period_invalid (a usage 'from' or 'to' that is not a timestamp, a period that is empty, or a summary or a count of unknown costs without both); 413 body_too_large; 415 unsupported_media_type; 409 period_start_backwards; 422 the other codes of a refused entitlement, among them cost_limit_requires_managed_key for a managed cost limit next to keyMode 'own' (the codes of the workspace entitlements validation, with 'field' naming the limit or key concerned), among them catalog_entry_invalid for a modelAccess that is not {catalogEntries} with null or at most 100 catalog entry ids ('field' is modelAccess or modelAccess.catalogEntries); 422 also invalid_token (a handoff token that is unknown, used, expired, revoked or whose person lost the role: one answer for all) and the codes of a refused plan management address (url_invalid, url_not_https, url_has_credentials, url_has_fragment, url_too_long); the codes of the removed model tier configuration (model_id_invalid, MODEL_UNKNOWN and the DYNAMIC_MODEL_* codes) went with its route (#434); 500 internal_error.

field.description: For a refused entitlement: the limit or the unknown key concerned (never its value).

EntitlementLimits.description: Every limit is required on a write; null is unlimited.

diffRunsPerPeriod.description: A count (or micro-USD of measured model cost) per period, or null for unlimited.

dynamicRunsPerPeriod.description: A count (or micro-USD of measured model cost) per period, or null for unlimited.

managedCostLimitMicroUsd.description: Micro-USD of measured model cost per period for the runs on the operator's key, or null for unlimited. A soft cap. Refused next to keyMode 'own' (cost_limit_requires_managed_key).

ownKeyCostLimitMicroUsd.description: Micro-USD of measured model cost per period for the runs on the workspace's own key (#361), or null for unlimited. A soft cap: a run that starts below it can end above it by what the runs in flight cost, and a run whose cost is unknown is not bounded by it. Entries stored before the limit existed read as null.

EntitlementLimitsWrite.description: The limits of a write: every limit, and no other key (a typo is refused with limits_invalid).

diffRunsPerPeriod.description: A count (or micro-USD of measured model cost) per period, or null for unlimited.

dynamicRunsPerPeriod.description: A count (or micro-USD of measured model cost) per period, or null for unlimited.

managedCostLimitMicroUsd.description: Micro-USD of measured model cost per period for the runs on the operator's key, or null for unlimited. A soft cap. Refused next to keyMode 'own' (cost_limit_requires_managed_key).

ownKeyCostLimitMicroUsd.description: Micro-USD of measured model cost per period for the runs on the workspace's own key (#361), or null for unlimited. A soft cap: a run that starts below it can end above it by what the runs in flight cost, and a run whose cost is unknown is not bounded by it. Entries stored before the limit existed read as null.

ModelAccess.description: Which catalog entries a workspace on the operator's key (keyMode 'managed') may use, by the ids of the entries as the admin portal shows them. catalogEntries null: every released entry. []: none. A list: those entries. An id that no entry has is accepted and matches nothing; an id listed twice is refused on a write. Next to keyMode 'own' it is accepted and kept but never read: a workspace on its own key chooses provider and model freely and reads no catalog.

EntitlementsFields.description: What an operator allows a workspace, as read back. 'modelAccess' (#428) is optional in an answer: an instance of an earlier release does not send it, so a reader that validates strictly must accept an answer without it during a rollout, and treats a missing field as {"catalogEntries": null} (every released entry), which is what such an instance grants. An upgraded instance always sends it. A write has its own rule (EntitlementsWrite).

planLabel.description: A label for display and audit, 1 to 64 printable characters. The app never branches on it.

keyMode.description: Whose LLM key the workspace's reviews use. 'managed' is the operator's key.

suspensionCode.description: Why the workspace is suspended: lowercase letters, digits, '_' and '-', starting with a letter, at most 64 characters. null unless suspended.

EntitlementsWrite.description: The body of PUT /workspaces/{id}/entitlements and PUT /entitlements/default: the whole entitlements, replacing what was stored, except 'periodStart' and 'modelAccess', which are kept when left out (see below). Unknown keys are refused (a typo must not pass). 'periodStart' may be left out: the stored start is kept, or the period starts now when nothing is stored. A start earlier than the stored one is refused (period_start_backwards, 409) and one more than five minutes ahead as period_start_in_future. A write is idempotent. A numeric limit above 2^53-1 is refused (limit_invalid) instead of being rounded. Removing a workspace's row (DELETE) ends the 'never backwards' guard for that workspace: a later PUT without periodStart begins now. A managed cost limit (managedCostLimitMicroUsd, even 0) next to keyMode 'own' is refused (cost_limit_requires_managed_key): it only counts runs on the operator's key, so it would never be read. An entry of that shape that was stored earlier keeps working: it is read as before and the limit is ignored. The workspace's own key has its own cost limit, ownKeyCostLimitMicroUsd (#361), which is allowed with either key mode and decides by the key a run actually used; every write states it, an entry stored before it existed reads it as null. 'modelAccess' (#428) may be left out: the stored value is kept (a write of an older writer never clears what was granted), a row that has none starts with every released entry, and {"catalogEntries": null} clears it. This is deliberately not 'replace everything' (unlike ownKeyCostLimitMicroUsd, which every write states): it needs no cutover, as 'periodStart' needs none. A PUT /entitlements/default without it over a stored default that cannot be read is refused as catalog_entry_invalid (field 'modelAccess'): there is nothing to keep, and only a write that states it repairs the default. The list holds each id once (a repeated id is refused as catalog_entry_invalid). Roll out in this order: upgrade every app instance first, because an instance of an earlier release refuses the unknown key (422 entitlements_invalid, field modelAccess) as it refuses any typo, then let the writer send it.

planLabel.description: A label for display and audit, 1 to 64 printable characters. The app never branches on it.

keyMode.description: Whose LLM key the workspace's reviews use. 'managed' is the operator's key.

suspensionCode.description: Why the workspace is suspended: lowercase letters, digits, '_' and '-', starting with a letter, at most 64 characters. null unless suspended.

InvalidEntitlements.description: A stored entry that cannot be read. It counts as 'invalid' for enforcement (fail closed); a valid PUT repairs it.

StoredEntitlements.description: The row of a workspace, with the time of its last write. Who wrote it is not part of the format.

EffectiveEntitlements.description: What applies to the workspace on its next claim: its own row, else the default, else nothing (unlimited: own key, no limits, not suspended). A running job is not touched.

EntitlementsSource.description: 'workspace': the workspace's own row. 'default': the instance default.

WorkspaceList.description: GET /workspaces?after=<id>&limit=<1..200, default 50>: workspaces ordered by id after the cursor. 'nextAfter' is the id to pass as 'after' for the next page, null on the last page.

WorkspaceEntitlementsResponse.description: The answer of GET, PUT and DELETE /workspaces/{id}/entitlements: the stored row (null when none, e.g. after DELETE) and the effective entitlements.

DefaultEntitlementsResponse.description: The answer of GET and PUT /entitlements/default: the default for workspaces without a row, an invalid marker for damaged data, or null when none was set. The default cannot be removed through the API.

UsageCursor.description: An opaque position in the usage feed: keep the 'nextCursor' of an answer and pass it back as 'after'. Do not parse it or build one; one the API did not write is refused with cursor_invalid. At most 128 characters of base64url.

UsageReason.description: Why a record carries no measurement, as a short code (lowercase letters, digits and '_'), or null. A reader ignores a code it does not know. 'no_result': the job ended without any result from the runner that held it (it died, its lease ran out on the last attempt, it ran past the hard limit), so the model may have been used and the cost and the tokens are unknown. A run that reported its usage, failed or not, carries no reason; an unpriced run has a null cost and its tokens. 'superseded' (#397): a newer push replaced the run while it ran. It is not a run of the free quota, but what it measured is usage like any other: the cost and tokens are those it reported (or both unknown, when its Worker never reported) and are billed like the cost of any run, an unknown cost never.

UsageItem.description: One settled run. Nothing about the pull request, the repository, the branch, the title or any person is in it, 'modelTier' is the name of a quality tier of a run from before the model catalog (null for newer runs), and 'catalogEntryId' / 'catalogEntryName' name the catalog entry a managed run used (null for an own-key run and for older runs); none of them is ever the name of a model. 'costMicroUsd' is millionths of a US dollar of measured model cost, null when the run could not be measured (never a guess); the token counts are null when unknown. A record is immutable once it is served.

id.description: The id of the record: the idempotency key. A reader that is handed a record twice (it retried a page) keeps one.

jobId.description: The id of the review job the record belongs to; one record per job.

reviewKind.description: Which review the run was. `implementer` is a turn of the Implementer (the factory deployment only, #752); a deployment without that capability never reports it.

keyMode.description: Whose LLM key the run used. 'managed' is the operator's key.

modelTier.description: Deprecated since the model catalog (#432, #434): the quality tier of a managed run from before the catalog, or null, and always null for a newer run (see catalogEntryId). Kept, required and nullable, so that a strict reader keeps working. Only a tier name is ever shown (lowercase letters, digits, '_' and '-', starting with a letter, at most 32 characters); anything else is served as null.

catalogEntryId.description: The catalog entry a managed run used (#432), or null for a run on the workspace's own key and for a run from before the catalog. Optional: an instance of an earlier release does not send it.

catalogEntryName.description: The name of that entry when the run was claimed (a rename does not rewrite history), or null. Never a model id.

UsagePage.description: GET /usage?after=<cursor>&limit=<1..200, default 50> (every workspace) and GET /workspaces/{id}/usage?after=&limit=&from=&to= (one workspace; 'from' included and 'to' excluded, on 'settledAt'): a page of SETTLED records ordered by (settledAt, id) after the cursor. Records that are reserved or void are never served. A record is served only once its 'settledAt' is more than 60 seconds old (the safety lag), so a record that commits late cannot appear behind a position a reader already holds; a reader that polls therefore sees the newest minute of settlements a little later. 'nextCursor' is the position after the last item, or the cursor that was passed when the page is empty, or null when nothing has been served and none was passed: keep it and pass it as 'after' next time. Treat 'id' as the idempotency key: keep one item per id, however often a page is read.

UsageSummaryGroup.description: What one workspace ran in the period, for one kind of review and one key mode. 'recordCount' counts the runs that count towards a limit (running or settled; void runs are left out), 'settledCount' those among them that are settled, 'supersededCount' the runs a newer push replaced (#397: they are not counted in 'recordCount' or 'settledCount', but their known cost is in 'knownCostMicroUsd' and their unknown costs in 'unknownCostCount'), 'knownCostMicroUsd' adds up the cost of the settled runs whose cost is known, and 'unknownCostCount' counts the settled runs whose cost is not known (they add nothing to the sum).

UsageSummaryResponse.description: GET /workspaces/{id}/usage/summary?from=&to=: both are required timestamps with 'from' before 'to'. A run belongs to the period it started in ('from' included, 'to' excluded), the same rule the limits count by, so this summary is what a limit sees; it is not a view of the feed (which is by time of settlement) and a run still in progress is counted in 'recordCount'. The groups are ordered by review kind then key mode; a combination without runs is not listed. The summary counts by the time a run started ('reserved_at'), so it does not reconcile with the feed, which is by time of settlement, at the edges of a period (a run that started on the 30th and settled on the 1st is in the earlier period's summary and the later period's feed). A closed period's counts can still change until its last run has ended: 'recordCount' minus 'settledCount' is the number still in progress. For accounts by time of settlement, use the feed.

UnknownCostCount.description: How many runs of one workspace on one key mode settled without a known cost in the period: a plain integer, with no cost figure, model, key or name. A cost limit adds up known costs only, so these runs are not bounded by it. 'keyMode' says whose key they ran on ('managed' is the operator's key), which decides which cost limit they escape.

UnknownCostCountsResponse.description: GET /usage/unknown-cost?from=&to=&after=<workspace id>&limit=<1..200, default 50>: both 'from' and 'to' are required timestamps with 'from' before 'to', and the answer lists, per workspace and key mode, the settled runs of the period whose cost is not known. This includes a run that ended with no result from its runner (reason 'no_result' in the feed). A run belongs to the period it started in ('from' included, 'to' excluded), the same rule the limits and the summary count by, so a figure here equals 'unknownCostCount' in the summary of that workspace, added up over the review kinds of a key mode. It is a total, not a position in the feed: there is no safety lag, and a run that is still in progress is not counted until it settles, so the count of a period can still grow until its last run has ended; to alert on a rate, read the same period again and compare. Ordered by workspace id, then key mode. A workspace and key mode without such a run is not listed, so a workspace that is missing has a count of zero. A page holds the counts of up to 'limit' whole workspaces after 'after'; 'nextAfter' is the workspace id to pass as 'after' for the next page, null on the last page.

PlanManagementWrite.description: The body of PUT /plan-management: the address of the page a workspace Owner or Admin is handed over to when they click 'Manage plan' in the app. It has to be an absolute https address without user name, password or fragment; it is stored in its normal form. Anything else is refused with 422 and one of the url_* codes. Unknown keys are refused (400 request_invalid).

PlanManagementResponse.description: The answer of GET, PUT and DELETE /plan-management: the address in its stored form, or null while there is none. While there is none, the app shows no 'Manage plan' button and its route does not exist. The app appends the single query parameter 'handoff=<token>' to this address when it hands somebody over (any 'handoff' parameter in the stored address is replaced); the page that receives it redeems the token at once with POST /handoff/redeem and does not keep it in its address bar, its logs or its links.

HandoffRedeemRequest.description: The body of POST /handoff/redeem: the token from the 'handoff' query parameter. Exactly this key. A token of any other shape is not a request error: it gets the same invalid_token answer as an unknown one.

HandoffRedeemResponse.description: The answer of POST /handoff/redeem for a valid token: which workspace the person who clicked 'Manage plan' belongs to and with which role. A token is valid for five minutes after the click and works once; a newer click of the same person in the same workspace revokes it; the role is checked again at redemption (a person who is no longer a member with the role the token was made for gets invalid_token, and the token is used up). 'userId' is opaque: the same person always has the same id, and it is nothing an email, a name or a repository could be recovered from. Nothing else about the person is ever served. The service redeems the token before it shows anything, and sends the person back to /w/<workspaceSlug>/settings/plan of the app (the plan and usage page of the workspace); that path is fixed on the app's side.
